learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will develop essential reading strategies, including skimming, scanning, and inferencing, to effectively analyze and answer questions based on unfamiliar texts.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Imagine being a detective handed a secret document you've never seen before. Your mission? Find the hidden clues, understand the main plot, and answer the questions! That's exactly what reading comprehension is all about. Put on your detective hat!

lesson_modules.module_title: 👁️ Skimming and Scanning (सरसरी निगाह और खोजना)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Skimming means reading very fast just to get the 'main idea' of the passage (read the first and last sentences of paragraphs). Scanning means hunting for specific details like a date, a name, or a number without reading every single word.
examples_or_templates: Skimming: Quickly glancing over a news article to see if it's about sports or politics.
Scanning: Looking at a train timetable strictly to find the number '10:30 AM'.

lesson_modules.module_title: 🧠 Finding the Main Idea (मुख्य विचार को समझना)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Every paragraph has a core message. To find the main idea, ask yourself: 'What is the author mostly talking about here?' The topic sentence (usually the first sentence) often gives it away.
examples_or_templates: Passage: 'Bees are vital to our ecosystem. They pollinate flowers, which helps crops grow. Without them, we would lose a lot of our food.'
Main Idea: The importance of bees for food production.

lesson_modules.module_title: 🕵️‍♂️ Inference and Context Clues (निष्कर्ष और सुराग)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Sometimes the answer isn't written directly in the text. You have to 'read between the lines' (infer). Also, if you find a word you don't know, look at the words around it (context clues) to guess its meaning!
examples_or_templates: Inference text: 'Rohan grabbed his umbrella and raincoat.' -> Inference: It is raining outside.
Context clue text: 'The diamond was **flawless**, containing absolutely no scratches or marks.' -> Flawless means perfect/without marks.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ If you are quickly looking through a passage to find the year a scientist was born, which strategy are you using?
❓ Read: 'The dog growled, bared its teeth, and the hair on its back stood up.' What can you infer?
options: The dog is angry or threatened.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: The dog is angry or threatened.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ What is the main idea of this sentence: 'Despite the heavy rain, fierce winds, and dark skies, the brave team continued climbing the mountain.'
subjective_practice.hint: Is it about the weather, or about the determination of the climbers?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Use context clues to guess the meaning of the bold word: 'He was **famished** because he hadn't eaten anything for two days.'
subjective_practice.hint: Look at the reason given. What happens when you don't eat for two days?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Explain the difference between skimming and scanning in one sentence.
subjective_practice.hint: One is for the 'big picture', the other is for 'specific details'.

activity_or_assignment.title: ⏱️ The 60-Second Scan Challenge
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Take a random page from a newspaper or a magazine. Ask a parent to pick a specific word, number, or name from that page. Time yourself to see how many seconds it takes you to 'scan' the page and point to the exact word!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Skimming is reading quickly to find the main idea; Scanning is looking for specific facts or details.
⭐ The Main Idea is the central point the author is trying to make in a paragraph.
⭐ Inferencing means using clues from the text and your own knowledge to guess things not explicitly written.
